hlni.insight: Core subjects in business degrees are often standardized; the elective bank is the primary variable for personalization.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume B.Com and BBA have fundamentally different curricula without checking elective depth.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewer shifts from comparing degree titles to auditing specific elective modules against their own interests.
hlni.support: The method encourages mapping personal curiosity to course offerings, acknowledging that elective availability dictates specialization potential.
hlni.payoff: The viewer gains a tangible tool to evaluate their own academic path, moving beyond stereotypes.

candidate.reelTitle: The Curriculum Puzzle: B.Com vs BBA
candidate.creativeAngle: An interactive 'Curriculum Puzzle' that challenges the viewer to look past core modules to elective variety.
candidate.objective: Empower students to compare degrees by evaluating elective flexibility rather than just broad labels.
candidate.targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Hook
shots.visual: A split screen shows two identical lists labeled 'Core Curriculum'. A cursor hovers, confused.
shots.dialogue: Think B.Com and BBA are totally different? Look closer.
shots.onscreenText: B.Com vs BBA: Spot the difference?

shots.name: The Pattern Interrupt
shots.visual: An animation shows 'Interest Blocks' like 'Data' and 'Strategy' being dragged into a grid. They fit into both.
shots.dialogue: Core subjects often overlap. The real difference isn't the name, it's the elective bank.

shots.name: The Method
shots.visual: A hand checklist appears: '1. List interests. 2. Check elective bank. 3. Count the matches.'
shots.dialogue: List your top three interests, then check the elective bank. See which degree lets you build your own path.
shots.onscreenText:
1. List Interests 
2. Check Electives 
3. Count Matches

shots.name: The Payoff
shots.visual: The student smiles, looking at a customized list of subjects.
shots.dialogue: A degree is only as good as the electives that match your curiosity.
shots.onscreenText: Choose by curiosity, not just the title.

productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts synced to drag-and-drop sounds.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the student's focus from degree labels (B.Com/BBA) to elective availability to ensure academic agency.

selected.title: The 'Curriculum Puzzle'
selected.audienceGap: Ignoring the 'Elective' portion of a degree which often holds the real difference.
selected.hlni: The 'core' subjects are often identical; the flexibility of electives is where the degree's true character is found.
selected.viewerChange: Changes the search criteria from 'Core subjects' to 'Elective variety'.
selected.concept: A visual puzzle where the viewer tries to 'fit' their interests into a degree structure.
selected.device: Interactive visual where the viewer drags 'Interest Blocks' (e.g., Data, Strategy, Finance) into a degree grid.
selected.support: Encourages matching personal interest to elective availability; limited by general availability of choices.

selected.interpretationRule: A degree is only as good as the electives that match your curiosities.

selected.payoff: The viewer realizes they have agency in customizing their education.
selected.limitations: Elective availability is subject to university scheduling and capacity.

comparedWith.hlni: Degrees are distinguished by the 'Assessment Outcome'—what the student is specifically asked to demonstrate (e.g., technical accuracy vs. process-based application).
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of two anonymous task descriptions, highlighting the specific verbs used (e.g., 'Calculate/Report' vs 'Propose/Defend').

comparedWith.hlni: The difference isn't the subject, it's the 'lens' applied (e.g., a B.Com student looks at the *cost* of a campaign, a BBA student looks at the *execution* of the campaign).
comparedWith.device: A single business case study presented from two distinct analytical viewpoints.
